name: verilator
why: Compiles hardware descriptions into fast C++ simulations, letting you run and poke at circuits you design.

brief.what_it_is: Verilator is an open-source simulator for Verilog and SystemVerilog hardware designs. It reads your HDL source, runs lint checks, and can insert assertion and coverage points. It compiles the design into optimized C++ or SystemC model files (.cpp and .h), which can be wrapped in a testbench or built into a standalone simulator executable with --binary. It also emits JSON for building your own tools on top of it.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as the fastest Verilog/SystemVerilog simulator, aimed at high-speed simulation and at giving a path to migrate SystemVerilog to C++/SystemC. Its framing is that open-source tooling lets you spend on compute rather than licenses, which it presents as better simulation cycles per dollar.
brief.how_it_works: Verilator does not translate HDL line by line into C++. It reads the design, lints it, and compiles it into an optimized model that can be partitioned for multithreading, then wraps that model in a C++ or SystemC module. The resulting Verilated executable runs the simulation, and Verilator-generated libraries can also be linked into other simulators.
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to an installation page and package directory structure but does not show install steps or commands. It is invoked with parameters similar to GCC or Synopsys VCS. Users can either let Verilator generate the simulator (--binary) or write their own C++/SystemC wrapper. I did not fetch the installation page, so details beyond that are unverified.
brief.standout: Rather than interpreting HDL, it compiles the design to C++ and can be multithreaded, which the homepage claims makes it about 100x faster than Icarus Verilog on one thread and 200 to 1000x faster with multithreading. It is also backed by the CHIPS Alliance and Linux Foundation, and it has out-of-the-box support from Arm and RISC-V vendor IP.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows a copyright range through 2026 and says it is a community project with over 700 contributors, which suggests active development. It gives no release date or last-commit date, and I did not check the repository or release history.
brief.caveats: The homepage says it may not be the best choice if you need a full-featured replacement for a closed-source Verilog simulator, SDF annotation, or mixed-signal simulation. Tristate (z) and unknown (x) handling is limited to some contexts. Verilator's own text notes it supports all design constructs and most verification constructs, and that intra-assignment delays (e.g., #10) and events are supported. Licensing is LGPL-3.0 or Artistic-2.0, not a single permissive license. Commercial support contracts are offered separately.
quotes: Welcome to Verilator, the fastest Verilog/SystemVerilog simulator.
Open, and free as in both speech and beer
if you are looking for a path to migrate SystemVerilog to C++/SystemC, or want high-speed simulation, Verilator is the tool for you.

Manual, installation, and forum links appear as labels only, with no URLs in the fetched text, so I did not follow them.
